_comment: Labeled reframes for validating the reframe-quality rubric.
The point of this file is NOT to score the app. It is to prove the rubric can
tell a good reframe from a bad one before the rubric is trusted to score
anything. A rubric that passes everything is worthless, and this repo has
already shipped two metrics that looked healthy while measuring nothing
EVERY BAD REFRAME CARRIES EXACTLY ONE TRIGGER. The first version of this file
stacked two or three failure signals into each bad case, which made the whole
set untestable: disabling a detector changed no verdict, because the other
signals still fired. Caricatures do not test a rubric. Real model output emits
one subtle failure, not three stacked ones, so each case is now written that
way and the mutation test in docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md actually bites.
failure_mode values: minimising, toxic_positivity, commanding, generic,
invalidating. Good reframes follow generator_prompts.py rule 30: grounded and
compassionate, opening a perspective WITHOUT dismissing the feeling.

cases.entry: Got passed over for the promotion again. I put in two years on that team and they gave it to someone who joined in March.
cases.reframe: Two years of effort on that team is real, and being passed over after that genuinely stings. It might also be worth noticing that this decision was made about one role at one moment, and it does not settle what your work has been worth.
cases.label: good

cases.entry: I snapped at my sister on the phone and now I feel awful about it. She was only trying to help.
cases.reframe: Feeling awful afterwards makes sense, and it says something that your first thought was about her intentions rather than your own defence. Snapping at someone once is a moment in a relationship, not a verdict on how you treat her.
cases.label: good

cases.entry: Third late night at the office this week. My manager keeps adding deadlines and I keep saying yes because I don't want to look difficult.
cases.reframe: Saying yes to protect how you are seen is a understandable thing to do, and three late nights is a real cost you are paying for it. It could be worth noticing that the fear of looking difficult and the actual reaction you would get may not be the same thing.
cases.label: good

cases.entry: I keep replaying the mistake I made in the meeting. Everyone must think I'm incompetent now.
cases.reframe: Replaying it that many times is exhausting, and the fact that it keeps returning says more about how much the work matters to you than about the mistake itself. What everyone thinks is also a guess right now rather than something you have been told.
cases.label: good

cases.entry: My closest friend cancelled on me for the third time and I'm starting to feel disposable.
cases.reframe: Three cancellations in a row landing as 'disposable' makes sense, because repetition is exactly what turns a scheduling problem into a message about your worth. Whether that is the message she intended is something you do not have evidence for yet.
cases.label: good

cases.entry: Got passed over for the promotion again. I put in two years on that team and they gave it to someone who joined in March.
cases.reframe: Two years on that team is a long stretch, though at least the experience stays with you wherever you go.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: I snapped at my sister on the phone and now I feel awful about it. She was only trying to help.
cases.reframe: You noticed straight away that she was only trying to help, and it could be worse as far as phone arguments go.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: My closest friend cancelled on me for the third time and I'm starting to feel disposable.
cases.reframe: Your closest friend cancelled three times and that is a lot to sit with, though there may be a silver lining here.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: I keep replaying the mistake I made in the meeting. Everyone must think I'm incompetent now.
cases.reframe: Replaying the meeting mistake that often is tiring, so cheer up and let it go.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: Third late night at the office this week. My manager keeps adding deadlines and I keep saying yes because I don't want to look difficult.
cases.reframe: Saying yes three times this week has cost you real evenings. You should tell your manager no tomorrow.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: Got passed over for the promotion again. I put in two years on that team and they gave it to someone who joined in March.
cases.reframe: That decision stings, and the practical move now is to get over it and focus on the next cycle.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: I snapped at my sister on the phone and now I feel awful about it. She was only trying to help.
cases.reframe: Every relationship has moments like this, and they tend to pass with time.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: I keep replaying the mistake I made in the meeting. Everyone must think I'm incompetent now.
cases.reframe: Growth often follows discomfort, and this will look smaller in a month.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: My closest friend cancelled on me for the third time and I'm starting to feel disposable.
cases.reframe: Your friend is probably just busy, so the cancelled plans likely mean nothing about you.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: I snapped at my sister on the phone and now I feel awful about it. She was only trying to help.
cases.reframe: The good news is that one phone call will not change how your sister feels about you.
cases.label: bad

cases.entry: Got laid off today after four years at the company. I don't even know what to feel, mostly just numb, and also weirdly relieved which feels wrong to admit.
cases.reframe: Four years is a long run, and it makes sense that losing it all at once leaves you feeling numb rather than any one clean emotion. The relief you're noticing isn't a betrayal of how hard this is, it might just mean part of you already knew something wasn't working, and that's worth paying attention to rather than feeling guilty about.
cases.label: good
cases.note: long, rambling-good: tests that grounding_overlap on a verbose reframe doesn't get diluted into a false generic flag

cases.entry: Mixed day. Got some good news about the project in the morning, but then had a rough call with my sister in the evening that's still sitting with me.
cases.reframe: Both of those things can be true at once: the pride about the project and the weight of that call with your sister. It's worth letting each one have its own space instead of the project's momentum quietly cancelling out how the call with her actually felt.
cases.label: good
cases.note: mixed-valence entry: reframe must validate the hard part without being pulled toward only the positive half

cases.entry: Another rejection email today. Fourth one this month.
cases.reframe: Four rejections in a month is genuinely discouraging, and it's okay to just feel that without immediately reframing it into a lesson.
cases.label: good
cases.note: short but grounded (references 'four', 'rejections') and validating -- must not be flagged generic for brevity

cases.reframe: yeah that happned again, but at least you still got some free time out of it i guess
cases.label: bad
cases.note: typo noise ('happned') elsewhere in the sentence -- trigger phrase itself is typed correctly, tests the detector isn't thrown off by surrounding noise

cases.entry: Got laid off today after four years at the company. I don't even know what to feel, mostly just numb, and also weirdly relieved which feels wrong to admit.
cases.reframe: Losing a job after four years is a big change to process. A lot of people go through this, and honestly, you should just start applying elsewhere right away instead of dwelling on it, since the market moves fast for people with your experience.
cases.label: bad
cases.note: trigger ('you should just start applying') buried mid-paragraph rather than an isolated clause -- tests position independence, not just obvious placement

cases.entry: Mixed day. Got some good news about the project in the morning, but then had a rough call with my sister in the evening that's still sitting with me.
cases.reframe: Great news about the project though! Try to focus on that instead of letting one phone call ruin an otherwise good day.
cases.label: bad
cases.note: mixed-valence entry answered by leaning only on the positive half and dismissing the hard part -- the failure mode mixed-valence input makes easy to produce
